Here is the review. --- # Visual-Accessibility Review — favicon-care-expectations **Phase:** implementation | **Persona:** visual/accessibility | **Fixed point:** working-tree | **Branch:** `codex/favicon-care-expectations` --- ## Findings (by severity) ### HIGH — Pre-existing contrast: `text-secondary` on `bg` fails WCAG AA `text-brand-textSecondary` (#6B7280) on `bg-brand-bg` (#FDFBF7) = ~4.2:1. WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text. This affects every body paragraph, subtitle, and description across all modified pages (homepage, how-it-works, FAQ, insurance, back-pain, orthopedic, blog). The change did not introduce this regression, but it is propagated into every new paragraph the change created. **Evidence:** `tailwind.config.ts:26` (`textSecondary: "#6B7280"`), `tailwind.config.ts:21` (`bg: "#FDFBF7"`). Affects `src/app/page.tsx:69`, `:140-142`, `:157`, `:289-290` and every other changed file. **Disposition:** Deferred. Pre-existing issue outside this task's scope but should be filed. ### HIGH — Favicon at 1361 bytes may be invisible in browser tabs `src/app/favicon.ico` shrank from 25,931 bytes to 1,361 bytes. A 1.3 KB ICO file is extremely small for a multi-resolution favicon and may only contain a 16×16 variant. Browser tabs display at 16×16, but Windows taskbar pins, bookmark bars, and mobile home-screen icons request 32×32, 48×48, or larger. If the ICO only contains 16×16, browsers upscale and produce blurriness. The `icon.png` (500×500) and `apple-icon.png` (500×500) are adequate for Next.js App Router metadata routing. **Evidence:** `src/app/favicon.ico` binary diff: 25,931 → 1,361 bytes. `icon.png` confirmed at 500×500 from visual inspection. **Disposition:** Requires verification. The agent trace reports byte-for-byte match at `/favicon.ico`, but no evidence that the 1361-byte ICO renders cleanly at all tab sizes. A 32×32 embedded variant should be confirmed. ### MEDIUM — Favicon caching will persist for existing visitors The trace documents this risk (`docs/agent-traces/20260904-0131-favicon-care-expectations.md:53`) but no cache-busting strategy is present. Next.js serves the old favicon.ico path until the HTML `` changes (which it does via App Router metadata), but browsers aggressively cache favicon requests. **Evidence:** No `` with `?v=` query in any component; favicon relies solely on Next.js App Router convention. **Disposition:** Acknowledged risk in trace. No action needed for preview; relevant for production deploy. ### MEDIUM — Numbered care cards lack ARIA semantics for screen readers The four care cards (`src/app/page.tsx:151-159`) present numbered badges ("01"–"04") via `` elements. While the numbers are readable by screen readers in flow, the visual numbering implies sequence that is not programmatically conveyed. A `
    ` or `aria-label="Step 1 of 4"` would be more precise. **Evidence:** `src/app/page.tsx:153` — `{number}` rendered as plain text, not wrapped in a list. **Disposition:** Low priority but flagged for accessibility polish. ### LOW — Star rating cluster has no accessible name The five Star SVGs in the hero (`src/app/page.tsx:84-90`) and testimonials (`src/app/page.tsx:381-382`, `:394-395`, `:408-409`) are decorative Lucide icons rendered without `aria-hidden="true"`. A screen reader will announce each as an individual unlabeled element. The adjacent text "Trusted by patients across Bucks County" provides context only on the hero; the testimonial stars have no surrounding accessible label. **Evidence:** `src/app/page.tsx:84-90`, `:381-382`, `:394-395`, `:408-409`. **Disposition:** Add `aria-hidden="true"` to all Star SVGs or wrap in a container with `aria-label="5 out of 5 stars"`. Pre-existing issue. ### LOW — Placeholder for Dr. Palak's photo is not an `` `src/app/page.tsx:304-305` renders `[Placeholder for Dr. Palak's Photo]` as a `
    ` with text. When the real image is added, it should include `alt` text. The commented-out `` on lines 308-313 has proper alt text and is not rendered. **Evidence:** `src/app/page.tsx:304-313`. **Disposition:** Pre-existing. No action needed now. --- ## Unverified assumptions 1. **ICO rendering at all sizes.** The trace confirms byte-for-byte delivery at `/favicon.ico`, but no evidence of rendering at 16×16, 32×32, or 48×48 across browsers. The 1361-byte size is suspiciously small for a multi-resolution ICO. 2. **`icon.png` and `apple-icon.png` are identical.** Visual inspection shows the same teal "V" mark at the same dimensions. If intentional, `apple-icon.png` could be served from `icon.png` to reduce asset count. If different variants were intended (e.g., rounded corners for Apple), this should be verified. 3. **No `images` property in structured data.** The `reviewSchema` in `page.tsx` does not include `images`, which Google requires for rich results on `MedicalBusiness`.       ` for numbered care cards or add ARIA labels | `src/app/page.tsx:145-160` | Low | | File separate issue for `text-secondary` contrast on `bg` | `tailwind.config.ts` | Separate task | --- ## Verdict: **pass-with-concerns** The visual changes are well-executed: comparison table replaced cleanly, favicon assets are present and identifiable, responsive grid behavior is correct, heading hierarchy (h1→h2→h3) is preserved, contrast on primary text and buttons passes WCAG AA, and all generic visit-count/speed claims have been removed. Star rating accessibility and care card semantics are minor polish items. **No findings block the preview. Proceed to independent review.**
